content.text:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `performance` (performance): Load the CPU like a busy mid-range phone, then scroll the screen and use its slowest action; the UI must never freeze, and a key press during the action must not end in an ANR.
Steps: [{"fault": "cpu_stress", "threads": 4}, {"scroll": "down"}, {"scroll": "up"}, {"tap": "product_1"}, {"poke": true}, {"wait": 6}, {"poke": true}, {"settle": 8.0}]
Result: anr: application not responding: Input dispatching timed out (49c2d7b com.shubhasai.monkeymart/com.shubhasai.monkeymart.MainActivity is not responding. Waited 5003ms for MotionEvent).
Crash: ANR @ com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.ShopScreenKt$ShopScreen$4$1$2$1$1.invoke(ShopScreen.kt:56)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.ShopScreenKt$ShopScreen$4$1$2$1$1.invoke(ShopScreen.kt:56)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.ShopScreenKt$ShopScreen$4$1$2$1$1.invoke(ShopScreen.kt:56)

## Diagnosis
Root cause: The clickable modifier on each shop row runs `Thread.sleep(7000)` on the main thread before calling `onProductClick` (ShopScreen.kt:56). Each tap therefore blocks the UI thread for 7 s. Under cpu_stress the input dispatch waits on that handler, so the next key/motion event times out at 5 s and Android reports an ANR. The trace matches: a 7001 ms `dispatchInputEvent MotionEvent UP` slice on the main thread, about 7000 ms of it in sleeping/blocked state, and the ANR stack top at ShopScreen.kt:56.
Fix approach: Remove the blocking call from the click lambda so it only forwards the navigation event: `.clickable { onProductClick(product.id) }`. If the 7 s wait stands in for real work (a fetch or validation before opening detail), move that work off the main thread into a coroutine on Dispatchers.IO, for example in a ViewModel or a `rememberCoroutineScope`, and navigate when it completes. Show a loading state in the meantime rather than freezing input.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/ShopScreen.kt:56 - `.clickable { Thread.sleep(7000); onProductClick(product.id) }` blocks the main thread inside the click handler; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/ShopScreen.kt:56 - the ANR stack's topmost app frame is this same line, ShopScreenKt$ShopScreen$4$1$2$1$1.invoke; Perfetto: `dispatchInputEvent MotionEvent UP` on the main thread (tid 25421, asai.monkeymart) lasts 7001 ms, and its main-thread state is sleeping/blocked for 7000 ms, matching the 7000 ms sleep; Perfetto: the main thread is sleeping/blocked for 22502 ms (92%) of the trace, which is the stalled input pipeline; the CPU stress itself accounts for only the 920 ms + 480 ms of waiting for CPU

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/ShopScreen.kt

## Regression test
Add an instrumented Compose test in src/androidTest, e.g. ShopScreenTapTest, with a ComposeTestRule that renders ShopScreen with a stub onProductClick and a ProductRepository that returns the eight products. It taps the node tagged product_1 and asserts the callback fires within about 1 s (waitUntil with a 1000 ms timeout). Before the fix the callback only fires after the 7 s sleep and the test fails; after the fix it passes. The test must not kill the process or revoke permissions.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

content.text:
I removed `Thread.sleep(7000)` from the row's click handler in `ShopScreen.kt:56`, so it now only calls `onProductClick(product.id)`. The sleep no longer blocks the main thread, and nothing was moved to a coroutine because the code gave no sign of real work behind it.

I added the regression test `ShopScreenTapTest` in `app/src/androidTest`. It renders `ShopScreen` and waits for `product_1` to appear. It then taps `product_1` and requires the callback to fire within 1 s (`waitUntil`) and the whole tap to take under 1.5 s. The test compiles. I haven't run it on a device. It uses the real `ProductRepository`, which already returns the eight products, so I didn't write a stub.
